programmes.label: Modern Greek Language and Culture (Nieuwgriekse taal en cultuur) at University of Amsterdam

exception.reason: Three independently organised directions were tested. Modern Greek language, literature and source-based cultural study fails because UCR offers no Modern Greek acquisition, translation, sociolinguistics, Greek-language media or Modern Greek literary sequence. Modern Greek history, society and identity has genuine comparative history, sociology and humanities methods, plus isolated ancient-Greek and Renaissance-Mediterranean content, but no sustained modern Greece, Cyprus or Byzantine-to-modern Greek sequence. Greece in Europe, the eastern Mediterranean and contemporary politics has European Union, international-relations, conflict and law frameworks, but no modern Greek politics, Greek-European relations or eastern-Mediterranean area-studies spine. In every direction, extending adjacent material to 23 non-PPD courses would change the object of study to generic European studies or global humanities. The missing language and regional content are academic substance rather than professional qualification, so no complete UCR response is claimed.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and Fall-2026-start availability. MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology and MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy study ancient Greece, while MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean centres Renaissance art and exchange; none supplies modern Greek history, society, politics or language. GOSHIST111/211/312 provide broad modern, imperial and research-historical foundations, and GOSSOCI111/212/214/311 provide social theory and qualitative inquiry, but no course centres modern Greece, Cyprus, Byzantine-to-modern continuity or Greek identity. GOSPOLI112/212/311/313 and GOSLAWJ212/312 provide comparative politics, international relations, EU institutions, conflict and legal frameworks without a Greece- or eastern-Mediterranean-specific sequence. MCCLITR111/112/211/212/312, MCCCOMM111/211/213/311/312, MCCMEDI111/112/311/312 and HCBCOGN312 provide literary, rhetorical, media and psycholinguistic methods, but no Modern Greek instruction, Greek literature, Greek sociolinguistics, translation or Greek-source interpretation. No workbook row supplies the missing Modern Greek language and area-studies core, so a defensible 24-course programme cannot be assembled.

candidateAssessment.concept: Modern Greek language, literature and source-based cultural study
candidateAssessment.assessment: Literature, rhetoric, media, psycholinguistics and humanities research offer real analytic methods, but UCR has no Modern Greek acquisition, reading, writing, speaking, translation, literature, media or source-based research. Generic language and cultural-analysis methods cannot supply the language and cultural object that organise this direction.

candidateAssessment.concept: Modern Greek history, society and identity
candidateAssessment.assessment: Modern history, sociology, qualitative research and ancient-Greek or Mediterranean courses are adjacent foundations. Their documented content does not provide a sustained sequence in modern Greek political and cultural history, Cyprus, Greek national identity, contemporary Greek society or Byzantine legacies. A complete curriculum would become general European or global humanities study.

candidateAssessment.concept: Greece in Europe, the eastern Mediterranean and contemporary politics
candidateAssessment.assessment: European Union politics, international relations, public international law, conflict studies and intercultural communication supply transferable frameworks. They do not teach modern Greek politics, Greek-European relations, eastern-Mediterranean regional dynamics or contemporary Greek social debates, so expanding them to a full programme would become generic European studies.
